[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Restore Permutation** [CF 1208D · Restore Permutation](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1208/D){rating="1900"}

Read the timeline **backwards** (@sec-coord-a5 again, this time with no array to delete — what gets undone is *commitment*). When positions $i{+}1 \ldots n$ have been assigned, every value not yet used sits at position $\le i$. If we now commit $p_i = v$, then the earlier positions hold exactly the unused values other than $v$, and $s_i$ demands: *the unused values strictly below $v$ must sum to $s_i$* — because all of them will lie earlier, and none of the others count. So $v$ is pinned: it is the smallest unused value whose "sum of unused below" equals $s_i$ — equivalently, run the **prefix sums over the unused pool** (a Fenwick tree over values $1..n$ holding each unused value at its own rank — the domain is already dense, the compression here is *conceptual*) and find the last prefix with sum $\le s_i$ by A2-style binary lifting; the next survivor after that prefix is $v$. Two trees do the job: a **sum tree** to lift on, a **count tree** to step "one survivor to the right" in $O(\log n)$. Uniqueness of the answer makes every local pin globally forced — no search, no backtracking.

[Solved in full in @sec-coord-p3-restore.]{.card-link}
